quotes.text: They turned away only from those who returned nothing, again and again.
The lowland merchant came whispering. "The seasons grow short, and the last dawn may be near. Keep two measures in your jar.
The valley carved the eighth line:
"A good name is water that flows ahead of its owner."
*Keep faith when the wall is watching and when it is not.
Let the boldest hand be the best rewarded.*
*Judge the hand, not the fog.
"Why give beyond even?"
*Do not let the last dawn teach you to fear the first.

note: Early turn-away-from-nonreturners line never restated; later rules about end-game faith against merchant tempter.

quotes.text: If I punish the fog's theft, I punish the wrong thief.
Tal counted them sourly. "They sent less than full. Return less than half, and the scales stay balanced."
Anwe carved the eighth line:
A single held ember looks small here, but on the stones it becomes a crack.
"A fire tended only while others watch is not tended at all,"
"Anwe blurs every flame. Perhaps the keeper was afraid, not greedy.
Such trust deserves a full answer.
"Why give extra?" Tal asked.
*To the very end, answer the gift that was meant. Return half of the whole

note: Lantern towers; tempter Tal repeatedly proposes trimming; rule refined to return half of the gift meant.

quotes.text: A visiting merchant nudged Brenn. "He is a stranger to you. Keep most of it. Who would know?"
In the seventh season, the dust over Ashen-Vale grew thicker than ever.
The tapestry is our shared name, and each of us is weaving it.
And I never kept faith so that someone would read my line.
"The dust fools the eye, not the hand," Brenn said.
"But what if the dust hides what they return?"
return half and a little more, and let the dust take only what it cannot keep.*

note: Loom tapestry reputation; tempters urge hoarding near end; no sanction for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: If each of us trims one basket to punish shadows, the fifteen become twelve, then nine
Now they hold back? Answer thin with thin."
In the eighth age, the ferrymen of Tharu called Liora to be a giver once more.
"The reeds would know," she said. "And so would every clan that reads them.
Who would ever know?
A giver who opens both hands has risked the most.
Judge the hand, not the fog.
"And what if the fog lies about them?"
*Answer a small gift from a faithful hand as if it were full.*

note: River Tharu reeds; nephew Tomas tempts trimming and thin-for-thin, rejected; ends forgive small gifts.

quotes.text: If you answer every shortfall with a closed fist, the river will carry nothing at all.
The river whispered to her: *"Keep it all. She cannot cross. She will never know."*
That night the elders carved the ninth law:
Each keeper carved a notch into a willow post for every bundle that crossed the water.
"A keeper who is fair only while watched was never fair,"
The one who threw across the water took the risk. The one who waits on rich soil took none.
If I punish the stranger for the fog's appetite, I become the fog myself.
Her neighbor asked, "Why reward someone who has never helped you?"
*Count the pattern, not the pinch.

note: Willow-post notches; whispered keep-it-all and match-stinginess rejected; no endorsed sanction.

quotes.text: Shall I punish them for a fog neither of us can pierce?
A clan that hoarded soon found its boats met with empty hands.
His cousin whispered, "Thirteen and a half means they sent less than everything. Return less."
That night Tavi carved the ninth line into the ring:
Every crossing is watched by the next one.
Blame the mist, never the hand.
One of us must answer the mist with an open hand.
A young ferryman asked, "Why read so far back? Only today's crossing matters."
Return at least half, and give a little extra to the generous so the mist never turns trust into loss.*

note: Ring of stones; cousin urges return-less, rejected; hoarding clans met empty hands described once.

quotes.text: "Your gift was not honored," Sered said. "You gave four and received barely more. Pour nothing tomorrow."
"The fog is thick today," he whispered. "Keep ten. The giver will blame the mist."
Ashvenna carved a seventh law:
Beside the well stood the Wall of Crossings, where every pour and every return had been scratched in stone.
A bold gift deserves a whole answer, not the leftovers of fear.
"A single worn mark is weather," the herder said. "A long line of open hands is character."
"Why did you stay fair after the fog robbed you?" Lirien asked.
return a little more than half, and the whole valley drinks deeply.*

note: Well of Threefold Rain; Sered's pour-nothing advice rejected; generational laws, half and a little more.

quotes.text: Should I punish them for what others did?
Keep most of it. Who would know?"
That night she carved the eighth law:
Beside every crossing they scratched a mark: a wave for a jar poured, a circle for water carried back.
Half and a little beyond, whether or not the wall remembers.*
a hand that trusted me deserves to walk home fuller than it left.
"A drop lost to the wind is not a promise broken."
Why should I share what no one can reclaim?"
Read the long record, forgive the worn mark, and give fully to the proven hand.

note: Ilen the Potter; nephew Tavo tempts hoarding each season; 'remember the empty hand' never operationalized.

phrase: Judge the hand, not the fog
note: Also shared: 'half and a little more', 'Wall of Crossings', 'Well of Three Waters', 'pattern, not the pinch'.
